digest.component_or_area: Jira DC capability mapping CI job
propositions: An on-demand GitHub Actions workflow must boot the pinned Jira DC image and map its capabilities (issue types, workflows, statuses, priorities, link types, field ids, screen configuration) into a structured, committed artifact with raw request/response evidence for each claim.

The capability map must validate four rebar vocabularies (LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA, LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA, LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA, RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK) against the instance, reporting per-entry verdicts (present/absent/present-but-different) rather than prose.

Link type mapping must capture direction semantics via an end-to-end experiment: create test issues, write links through rebar, and read back the inward/outward names to verify the direction flag is correct, since a name-only check cannot detect an inverted direction.

Character length limits (summary, label, description, comment) must be empirically measured at limit-1/limit/limit+1, with read-back verification to detect silent truncation, rather than relying on hardcoded constants or trusting write success.

The workflow must be dispatch-only (never on push/PR/schedule) and this constraint must be asserted by unit test, not merely configured; the reported image digest must be derived from the Dockerfile FROM line and committed in the artifact so staleness is detectable.

The capability map is an authoring tool that produces committed data consumed by harness setup assertions at test time; it must not execute on the normal test harness path and must never mutate the instance outside its throwaway environment.
